story.title: China's Ministry of State Security thrust into the spotlight by Nvidia CEO affair - CNBC

facts.text: From recruitment of U.S. students to allegations surrounding Nvidia's Jensen Huang affair, reports point to one Chinese intelligence agency: the Ministry of State Security.

The MSS appears to have gained political influence under Chinese President Xi Jinping to "strengthen China's protections against espionage and foreign infiltration," Greitens wrote last year in China Leadership Monitor.
The publication is run by Minxin Pei, non-resident senior fellow of the German Marshall Fund of the United States.

In September, State Security Minister Chen Yixin published a rare article in the cyberspace regulator's magazine about the need to improve artificial intelligence governance and prevent related security risks.

Beijing has increasingly targeted the U.S. tech sector in an attempt to narrow the gap in artificial intelligence capabilities, Matt Pearl, director of the strategic technologies program at the U.S.-based think tank Center for Strategic and International Studies, previously told CNBC.
CNBC was unable to independently verify the allegation or a connection to MSS.

However, the company has not announced a family succession plan or indicated that either child is being prepared to take over as CEO.Huang has reportedly said he does not believe in succession planning.Alleged Chinese intelligence links put Huang under scrutinyThe investigation follows reports that a businesswoman named Alice Huang was suspected of having links to China’s Ministry of State Security.The New York Times first reported the allegation, citing people briefed on intelligence circulated in a memo among Trump administration officials in the spring.

Its filings also warn that a failure to plan for succession, transfer knowledge and manage leadership transitions could affect strategic planning, execution and long-term performance.135691857Could Jensen Huang’s children eventually lead NvidiaThe Nvidia's CEO two adult children, Madison and Spencer, both work at Nvidia and hold senior positions.
Nvidia has long been closely tied to one person: Jensen Huang.
Its shares fell more than 4% on Monday, even as the broader market rallied sharply.Nvidia has no obvious replacement for Jensen HuangHuang’s influence at Nvidia goes well beyond his role as CEO.

Nvidia’s board has since launched an independent investigation into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence agency.The board has said it has confidence in Huang and has no reason to believe that national security or Nvidia’s secrets were compromised.
They had expected Huang to remain in the role for at least another 10 years.Huang owns just over 3% of Nvidia’s outstanding shares and is one of its 11 board members.

Both siblings earned more than $1.2 million in fiscal 2026, according to company disclosures cited by the newspaper.Reportedly Huang had told a close friend his dream was for one of his children to eventually run Nvidia.
Nvidia’s flat management structure gives senior leaders direct access to him, but it also means there is no obvious second-in-command.“Jensen is Nvidia.
Nvidia is Jensen,” Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon told CNBC.
Still, the investigation has brought renewed attention to Nvidia’s lack of a publicly identified successor.
Some US officials have raised concerns that Megaspeed may have been involved in smuggling Nvidia computing chips in violation of export controls.
Lawmakers from both parties have called for briefings, while Democrats have pushed for investigations and new legislation to prevent advanced AI chips from supporting China’s military.
